2) Tests for core auto-fix behavior: - tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts uses ESLint RuleTester to verify before/after behavior. - For require-story-annotation (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING): * Invalid case: `function autoFixMe() {}` -> output `/** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */\nfunction autoFixMe() {}` with a suggestion whose output matches the fix. * Additional invalid cases cover function expressions, class methods, TS declare functions, and TS interface method signatures, all with explicit expected outputs including an inserted single-line @story comment. * Valid cases confirm that already-annotated functions and methods are unchanged. - For valid-annotation-format (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT): * Invalid: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story` -> `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`. * Invalid: `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION` -> `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`. * Valid: already-correct `.story.md` path remains unchanged. - Tests executed via tool: `npm test -- --verbose --runTestsByPath tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts` ran `jest --ci --bail --verbose --runTestsByPath tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts` with no error output from the command, indicating this story’s test suite passes.
3) Implementation of missing-annotation auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE): - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts: - meta.fixable: "code" enabling ESLint --fix. - Annotated with `@story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md` and `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING`, `REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE`, `REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE` in meta comments. - create(context) obtains sourceCode, merges options, and delegates to buildVisitors, which in turn use helper report functions that provide fixes. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - STORY_PATH = "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md"; ANNOTATION = `/** @story ${STORY_PATH} */` — a fixed, simple template aligned with story text describing a built-in template. - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): * Uses hasStoryAnnotation(...) to avoid adding duplicates, with robust heuristics (JSDoc, preceding comments, parent chain, etc.) wrapped in try/catch. * Resolves target node via resolveTargetNode to correctly place inserted comments. * Calls context.report with messageId "missingStory", data { name, functionName }, and: - fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), - suggest: [{ desc: `Add JSDoc @story annotation for function '...'`, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget) }]. - reportMethod(...) behaves similarly for method-like nodes, using createMethodFix and preserving error context. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - createAddStoryFix(target) returns a fixer that computes a safe insertion point from target or its export parent and does: `fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([start, start], `${ANNOTATION}\n`)` — only adds a single-line @story JSDoc comment before the node, not touching any runtime code. - createMethodFix(...) inserts the same ANNOTATION before methods with indentation: `${ANNOTATION}\n `. - Both functions operate only on comment insertion and avoid modifying function bodies, satisfying safety and preservation requirements. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts: - Visitors for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, ArrowFunctionExpression, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and MethodDefinition all: * Check options.shouldProcessNode(node) (scope/exportPriority filtering). * Resolve targets and delegate to helperReportMissing/helperReportMethod, connecting ESLint events to the auto-fix logic.
4) Implementation of format auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - getFixedStoryPath(original: string): * Returns null when original includes ".." (skips path-traversal or ambiguous cases). * Returns null if original already ends with `.story.md`. * For `.story` suffix, appends `.md`. * For `.md` (not `.story.md`), replaces with `.story.md`. * Otherwise appends `.story.md`. => Implements only minimal suffix-normalization logic (`.story`/.`md` variants) and explicitly avoids unsafe transformations. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - meta.fixable: "code" with a comment: "This rule's fixable support is limited to safe @story path suffix normalization per Story 008.0..." and annotated with `@story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md`, `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE`, `REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE`. - createStoryFix(context, comment, fixed): * Gets full comment text, locates "@story" and the value substring via a regex. * Computes a narrow fixRange for just the path value. * Returns a factory producing a fixer that does `fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed)`. * Returns null if @story or its value cannot be located safely (TAG_NOT_FOUND_INDEX or regex failure). - reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(...): * If createStoryFix returns null, falls back to reportInvalidStoryFormat (no fix but error message). * Else calls context.report with messageId "invalidStoryFormat" and fix: fixFactory(). - validateStoryAnnotation(...): * Rejects empty/whitespace-only values without fix. * Uses collapseAnnotationValue and pattern tests to detect valid and invalid paths. * Uses getFixedStoryPath to compute a candidate fixed path. * Only when `fixed` is non-null and matches the story regex pattern does it call reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix; otherwise it reports without a fix. => Combined, this ensures fixes are applied only in simple, clearly safe cases, and surrounding comment formatting is preserved.
5) Integration into the ESLint plugin and toolchain (AC: Integration & User Experience): - src/index.ts: - RULE_NAMES includes "require-story-annotation" and "valid-annotation-format" among other rules. - Each name is dynamically loaded from ./rules/name, and rules[name] is populated with the module’s default export. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES defines default severities; both rules are registered and participate in recommended/strict configs. - This ensures that when the plugin is configured and `eslint --fix` is run, both rules are active and their `fixable` behavior is available per ESLint conventions. - The RuleTester-based tests simulate ESLint’s behavior across various node patterns and confirm fixes are predictable (consistent insertion of @story comments and consistent suffix normalization for paths), satisfying the user-experience acceptance criteria.
6) Documentation of auto-fix capabilities (AC: Documentation): - user-docs/api-reference.md: - Rule `traceability/require-story-annotation` description explicitly documents auto-fix behavior: * "When run with `--fix`, the rule inserts a single-line placeholder JSDoc `@story` annotation above missing functions, methods, TypeScript declare functions, and interface method signatures using a built-in template aligned with Story 008.0... fixes are strictly limited to adding this placeholder annotation without altering the function body or changing any runtime behavior." - Rule `traceability/valid-annotation-format` description documents format auto-fix behavior: * "When run with `--fix`, the rule limits changes to safe `@story` path suffix normalization only—for example, adding `.md` when the path ends with `.story`, or adding `.story.md` when the base path has no extension—using targeted replacements implemented in the `getFixedStoryPath` and `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix` helpers. It does not change directories, infer new story names, or modify any surrounding comment text or whitespace, in line with Story 008.0; more advanced path normalization strategies and selective toggles ... are not yet implemented." - These docs match the implemented logic and clearly explain which scenarios are auto-fixable and which require manual intervention.
7) Out-of-scope / future work acknowledged: - The story’s REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE are explicitly marked in the spec text as "Not yet implemented" and described as planned future enhancements. - Current implementation uses a simple built-in placeholder template and does not provide fine-grained toggles beyond standard ESLint rule enable/disable, which aligns with the story’s own description of the current iteration.
traceability.notes: All in-scope acceptance criteria for docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md are met. These capabilities are integrated into the ESLint toolchain (rules export fixable metadata, are loaded by src/index.ts, and behave correctly under RuleTester), and are covered by dedicated tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts, which run successfully.
